images.title: Row 1 and Row 2 of a 10 slit mat
images.purpose: Show the example of the concept in one picture: a row that goes 3 over, 2 under and repeats, and the next row that swaps over and under.
images.composition: A two row weave on ten slits with the row names on the left, each row's words printed next to it, a small legend for over and under, and one sentence at the bottom.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TOP LEFT: the title A mat with 10 slits in dark #1F2937 sans-serif bold (40 px), left edge at x 60, about y 60. THE GRID: exactly 2 rows by 10 columns of crossings, 20 cells in all, every cell a 100 by 100 px rounded square (corner radius 10 px) with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px) and 8 px between cells. Row 1 has its top at y 190, row 2 has its top at y 298; the 10 columns start at x 300 and end at x 1372 (cell c, counted from 1 at the left, starts at x 300 + 108 times (c minus 1)). A cell is TEAL #0072B2 where the strip goes over (the strip lies on top and shows), and CREAM #F5E6C8 where the strip goes under (the paper shows). Row 1, cells from the left: over, over, over, under, under, over, over, over, under, under (teal in cells 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8, cream in cells 4, 5, 9 and 10). Row 2 is the swap of row 1: under, under, under, over, over, under, under, under, over, over (teal in cells 4, 5, 9 and 10, cream in cells 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8). So there are 6 teal and 4 cream cells in each row, and 12 teal and 8 cream cells in all. ROW NAMES: the text Row 1 centred at x 175 and y 248, and the text Row 2 centred at x 175 and y 356 (40 px, dark). ROW WORDS: the text 3 over, 2 under (repeat), centred at x 836 and y 150, directly above row 1, and the text 3 under, 2 over (repeat), centred at x 836 and y 450, directly below row 2 (both 40 px, dark #1F2937). LEGEND, left aligned: a teal 56 by 56 px square at x 300, y 540 with the text over: the strip lies on top at x 380, y 568; a cream 56 by 56 px square with a thin dark outline at x 300, y 620 with the text under: the strip goes below at x 380, y 648 (36 px, dark). BOTTOM CENTRE, about y 750: one line of bold dark text, Row 2 swaps over and under in Row 1 (48 px), the largest text in the frame. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: A row is described by counting its over and under steps and saying repeat, and the next row swaps over and under.
images.description: Two rows of a 10 slit mat: Row 1 goes 3 over, 2 under and repeats, and Row 2 swaps over and under.
images.context: Concept image for Describing a Weave in Words. It follows the idea of the weave rows in your maths book (a row written as over and under steps with the word repeat) and uses the concept's own mat of 10 slits.
images.teaching_notes: Count the teal cells and the cream cells together with the child, group by group: 3 teal, 2 cream, 3 teal, 2 cream. The slip to watch: writing every slit one by one instead of counting the groups.

image_decisions.why: The 10 slit mat with Row 1 and its swap shows why a row can be said in words by counting groups and saying repeat.
